success_metrics.recommendation_ref: R1 (rebalance paid-search spend toward high-retention keywords)
success_metrics.metric: 90-day voluntary churn rate of paid-search cohorts
success_metrics.cadence: Monthly, measured on each closing monthly cohort
success_metrics.threshold: Gap to organic cohorts narrows from 8.4pp to under 5pp within two cohorts
success_metrics.reasoning: The recommendation targets acquisition quality, so the earliest honest read-out is the first full 90-day cohort acquired after the spend change; the 5pp threshold is half the observed gap.

success_metrics.metric: Share of new accounts with fewer than 5 events in first 30 days
success_metrics.reasoning: Leading indicator: engagement moves weeks before churn does, so this metric shows whether the intervention works before churn data can.

monitoring_specs.alert_condition: paid_search_90d_churn - organic_90d_churn > 10pp for any monthly cohort
monitoring_specs.evaluation_window: Each monthly cohort at 90 days, evaluated monthly
monitoring_specs.reasoning: Fires if the channel gap re-widens beyond the worst observed value, before it compounds across quarters.

monitoring_specs.alert_condition: Pro-tier monthly voluntary churn > 4.5% for two consecutive months
monitoring_specs.reasoning: The price-driven uplift should decay as grandfathered accounts cycle out; sustained elevation means ongoing price sensitivity, not a one-off event.

knowledge_base_entry.question: What drove the Q3 churn increase in the SaaS product?
knowledge_base_entry.answer_one_paragraph: Q3 churn was driven primarily by low-quality paid-search acquisition (8.4pp higher 90-day voluntary churn than organic, holding within every plan tier) and secondarily by the mid-quarter Pro-tier price increase, whose uplift is event-driven and tier-concentrated. Low 30-day engagement is the strongest early predictor of voluntary churn.
